articles.title: Mozilla asks UK CMA to consult on browser choice screens now | The Mozilla Blog

Mobile browsers are a key gateway to the internet for 56 million people in the UK. Smartphone users spend around half an hour a day in these apps, and opening a browser is the most common way they look up information online.
Yet most people are using a smartphone browser that was preinstalled and set as the default for them, without ever being asked which browser they would actually prefer.
Mozilla believes people deserve an active choice in the tools they depend on every day, which is why the latest proposals from the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) matter. We welcome the CMA’s plans to give people a choice of search service and are asking it to consult on browser choice now, so both screens can launch together.

Search choice screens would also appear in Chrome on other platforms, including through a major update for existing users. Some AI assistants would also be eligible to appear alongside search engines.

articles.title: There's always a patient zero: Defending the NetScaler front door before the patch
articles.summary:
Beyond the patch: Protecting your NetScaler gateway against future vulnerabilities
The recent disclosure of a major vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler pointed to a widespread weak point: a login page is an attack surface that can be used to compromise and access an application server. Indeed, the disclosures included an actively exploited flaw that allowed attackers to execute commands on affected gateways without signing in. As with any emergency patch, admins had to weigh cutting off or disrupting their users’ access with the risk of delaying a critical security update.
If you’re a NetScaler customer and you haven’t patched your instance, stop reading and go do that. This was a bad one. Once you’ve finished the patch, we’ll explore how to avoid a future fire drill by laying additional security controls.
This issue extends beyond NetScaler and can be applied to any internal application available on the Internet. Remote desktop portals, administrative consoles, and other publicly accessible authentication pages all deserve the same scrutiny: Does the intended audience require unrestricted Internet reachability? And can an attacker bypass this authentication check to reach the application's server?

articles.title: Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Improve TTFT for multi-turn agentic workloads with bi-directional KV transfer in vLLM
Multi-turn agentic workloads build on accumulated context as an agent reasons, invokes tools, and incorporates earlier results. With each new turn, the client resends the conversation history, including system instructions, prior prompts, tool results, and model responses, causing the growing context to be processed repeatedly. In Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation, each request is split across specialized nodes: the prefill node processes the prompt and builds its key-value (KV) cache, then the decode node retrieves those KV blocks and generates the response.
Conventional disaggregated serving, however, only transfers KV cache in one direction: from prefill to decode node. This one-directional flow creates two inefficiencies for multi-turn workloads. First, after generating a response, the decode node holds KV cache entries for both the prompt and the newly generated tokens. When processing the next turn, the prefill node cannot retrieve those entries, so it must recompute the KV projections for the previous response tokens. Second, the decode node maintains the session state while the prefill nodes don’t, increasing the probability of cache eviction for active sessions on the prefill nodes. On a full cache miss, the prefill node must recompute KV projections for the entire conversation history, including system instructions, prior user requests, tool results, and m…

articles.title: Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
articles.summary:
Amazon has signed an agreement with X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP) to fund the building of a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana. The proposed plant, which would replace the now defunct coal-fueled Breed Generating Station in Fairbanks, Sullivan County, aims to provide up to 960 megawatts of carbon-free energy for both the regional power grid and Amazon’s data centers.
Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
The proposed nuclear plant would provide 960 megawatts to power the grid — and Amazon’s data centers.
No timeline for construction or operation has been announced for the facility, which Amazon says “could” create 1,000 construction jobs and 100 permanent roles. The facility in Indiana is targeting to build 12 Xe-100 SMR’s, an advanced (but unproven) reactor that’s still undergoing development and licensing. These reactors can be cooled using either air, water, or a hybrid solution of both, which Amazon says should allow them to be deployed in water-constrained regions without impacting water demand in local communities.
Indiana also happens to be home to a famously expensive and uncompleted energy project called the Marble Hill Nuclear Power Plant. It was abandoned half-finished in 1983 after $2.5 billion had already been sunk into it, and has been under continued demolition since 2008. Terms for Amazon’s agreement in Fairbanks haven’t been disclosed, so we can’t compare the cost between the facilities.

articles.title: One Compromised Login Exposed Millions of California Students’ Records
articles.summary:
Personal information on current and former California public school students was copied from a file transfer system belonging to Educational Testing Service (ETS), according to the California Department of Education (CDE).
ETS is a nonprofit that handles state and federally mandated testing under a contract with the state. The organization supports California’s CAASPP and ELPAC assessment programs and relied on a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site to share testing data with CDE.
The organization spotted unauthorized activity on the site on September 25, but the earliest access dates back to late May.
“The investigation determined that an unauthorized party used a compromised login credential at various times during the period from May 22, 2026 to September 18, 2026 to access the SFTP site to copy files containing California student information,” according to the CDE’s breach notice.
No victim count has been provided, but the notice says, “Information about California students, including but not limited to all students enrolled in the three previous school years, was accessed and copied.”
CDE’s own enrollment figures put that in perspective: more than 5.7 million students were enrolled in California public schools in 2025-2026. The department’s incident FAQ notes that the impacted population also extends to students who left a California school as far back as 2006 and whose transfer to another school was not confirmed with CDE.

Il se disait prêt à « encaisser » si cela permettait à « des centaines » de collègues d’arrêter de faire semblant. Lundi soir, ses messages avaient été supprimés et son compte X avait disparu.

Il assure qu’un simple prompt (la consigne écrite qu’on donne à l’IA) suffit déjà pour obtenir des jeux sur mesure, « pour le meilleur ou pour le pire ».

Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
Today, we're announcing a preview of a new class of System One-style models: extraction models. Our first one, Clairic, is available hosted on Workers AI as @cf/cloudflare/clairic.We intend to release the model open-weights soon. Clairic is an extraction model that is able to extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs — all at a significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and cheaper cost than traditional LLMs.
Context
When System One models were announced by TypeSafe a month ago, it took the industry by storm. As referenced by TypeSafe in their blog and defined by Daniel Kahneman’s book Thinking, Fast and Slow, a System One model should be fast and precise, which contrasts a System Two model that is capable of deliberate reasoning (like LLMs). With this, TypeSafe introduced Jev — a model that is purpose-fit for a specific use case, and priced accessibly given its niche domain. articles.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) is a Python-based DSL and parallel programming model for NVIDIA GPUs that automatically leverages advanced hardware capabilities to deliver peak performance for tile-level GPU programming. By abstracting thread- and warp-level scheduling behind high-level, tile-centric primitives, cuTile enables you to write GPU kernels in Python while compiler optimizations automatically target advanced hardware features like Tensor Cores.
As an early adopter of cuTile, machine learning engineers at Jane Street implemented Mamba-2, a state-of-the-art sequence model, in cuTile and partnered with NVIDIA to optimize the kernels. Jane Street is a deeply technical global trading firm, using deep learning to drive innovation in advanced quantitative research. This post walks you through the three custom kernels powering the Mamba-2 forward pass and the cuTile optimizations behind them.
Overview and prerequisites
To use cuTile, ensure your environment meets the requirements outlined in the cuTile Python Quickstart guide. Import the package as cuda.tile and expose it as ct throughout the kernel implementations featured in this post.

articles.title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM
vLLM is an open-source inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). LLM inference has two distinct phases: prefill, which processes the input prompt and builds the key-value (KV) cache, and decode, which uses that cache to generate output one token at a time. These phases have different compute, memory, and scaling characteristics. Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation runs them on separate engine instances, allowing each phase to scale and be optimized independently. This can improve resource utilization, throughput, and latency under load. However, it also requires transferring the KV cache from the prefill instance to the decode instance before token generation can begin, making efficient KV transfer critical to time-to-first-token (TTFT).
One of the ways vLLM performs this transfer is through the NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library (NIXL) connector, which moves KV blocks over interconnects that support Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA), such as AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (AWS EFA, the low-latency RDMA network used across servers in AWS). On supported instance types, AWS EFA supports GPUDirect RDMA and Neuron Direct RDMA. NIXL can therefore transfer KV blocks directly between GPU or AWS Trainium device memory without staging through host memory. articles.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
articles.summary:
Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
When we previously blogged about our AI code reviewer in April, an average review cost a palatable $1.19. By the end of August, that figure had shot up to about $2.46. We hadn't made any significant architectural changes: the coordinator was still handing work to the same set of specialist reviewers, and the same risk tiers decided how intensive of a review we gave.
Around mid-September we tasked our agents with working out where those tokens were going and cutting them — aggressively. With code quality at high effort, the average review now costs just $0.77, down 68% from the $2.43 it averaged over our two most expensive weeks before we started. Our main goal was to cut costs, but as part of this work we also managed to optimize the reviewer, so that the median review now takes just 1m 32s instead of the 4m 09s it took before.
About 40% of the savings came from changes and optimizations to the reviewer's code, and the rest from experimenting with which models we use and how much effort they put in.

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:

- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: One pilot, two aircraft: F-22 Raptor directs autonomous combat drone in glimpse of future air warfare
articles.summary:
What just happened? The US Air Force has announced the military's latest move toward an autonomous future. This time, an F-22 Raptor pilot directed a drone during simulated combat. The pilot issued high-level tactical directives to the YFQ-44A while flying, essentially turning it into an unpiloted wingman.
The demonstration took place earlier this month, when the Raptor and Anduril's YFQ-44A Fury took off from Edwards Air Force Base in California.
Once airborne, the pilot sent an updated mission plan over a tactical data link. The drone's onboard software interpreted those instructions and carried out the maneuvers and simulated combat tasks.
While it might sound like it, this wasn't a case of someone flying two aircraft at once. The pilot decided what the Fury should do, while the autonomous system handled the flight controls.
The test was part of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program. The initiative's aim is to field low-cost, semi-autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles that fly alongside crewed fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets.
The test involved just one Raptor and one Fury, but the longer-term ambition is for a single pilot to direct several autonomous wingmen. Those aircraft could bring extra weapons, sensors, and electronic warfare equipment to a mission.

La France n’est d’ailleurs pas la seule à prendre son temps : ils ne seraient que cinq États, sur les vingt-deux à avoir officiellement franchi le pas (Italie, Danemark, Pays-Bas, Finlande et Portugal).

articles.title: The gap between financial inclusion and access to credit in Nigeria
articles.summary:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria has made progress in bringing more people into the formal financial system, but having a bank account does not necessarily mean being able to obtain a loan. While more Nigerians can now access financial services, borrowing costs, limited credit histories, and irregular incomes still shape who can obtain formal credit and on what terms.
According to the 2026 Access to Financial Services in Nigeria (A2F) survey by Enhancing Financial Innovation & Access (EFInA), formal financial inclusion rose to 73%, up from 64% in 2023. The proportion of adults excluded from the financial system fell from 26% to 21%. EFInA estimates that 87.2 million Nigerian adults are now formally included, yet only about 12 million (10%) access formal credit.
These figures show that financial inclusion is not the same as access to credit. Financial inclusion encompasses access to and use of services such as payments, savings, insurance and borrowing. A person may have a bank account, receive payments digitally and save through a formal institution without qualifying for a loan.
For lenders, they must determine whether a borrower earns enough to repay, whether that income can be verified, what other financial obligations the borrower has, and how likely they are to meet the repayment schedule…

articles.title: La ley y los expertos coinciden: puedes instalar un cepo en tu plaza de garaje para que tus vecinos no la ocupen

Buscaste una plaza de garaje porque en tu barrio es horrible aparcar. Llegas a las tantas de la noche de un día entre semana de tus cortas pero merecidas vacaciones. Dejas las cosas a la puerta de casa y mientras tu pareja las sube, tú vas llevando el coche a tu plaza de garaje. Pero cuando llegas, hay otro coche en tu plaza. No es broma. Son las once de la noche, al día siguiente madrugas y te encuentras dando vueltas por un barrio saturado de coches aparcados en la calle.
¿Cómo evitarlo la próxima vez?
No es broma. Aunque yo creía que sí. Prometo que no es una licencia literaria lo que voy a contar. Un día, tomando algo con un amigo me cuenta que el otro día llegó a casa y alguien había aparcado en su plaza de garaje. "Me quedé a cuadros porque no tenía sitio dónde aparcar fuera, en la calle", me dijo.
Después de conseguir aparcar y tras un par de horas enganchados al teléfono conectando llamadas consiguieron enterarse de que la persona que había aparcado era el hermano de una vecina. Se había equivocado de plaza de garaje porque había anotado mal el número de la misma y se había ido de viaje. Aprovechando que su hermana estaba también de vacaciones, tenía un garaje gratis en Madrid.
"Y tanto", me dijo mi amigo que recalcó entre risas un "como que lo estaba pagando yo". Por suerte, quedaba libre la plaza de la vecina y pudo aparcar sin problemas hasta que ésta volvió e hicieron el intercambio.

A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more.

Another, “cleanyourtv,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV.

Inside the quest to combat Arctic fires and save the planet’s frozen carbon
These scientists hope that fire-spotting satellites, AI tools and ancient land practices could preserve the world’s vulnerable permafrost—and the vast carbon it stores.
In the middle of an especially warm July in 2021, a wildfire ignited in a thick forest of black spruce and peeling paper birch trees on the northern campus of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks.
The blaze, possibly sparked by lightning, burned across the dry carpet of feather mosses and lichen before climbing into the crowns. By the time fire agencies responded, flames had reached 12 feet in length and sent up a 500-foot column of smoke.
A few days shy of the five-year anniversary of the Yankovich Road Fire, I followed three members of the Alaska Fire Science Consortium into the boreal forest, walking along cross-country ski trails lined by feathery field horsetail.

F5 has released out-of-band security patches to address multiple NGINX web server flaws, including three critical-severity vulnerabilities that can let attackers execute code on vulnerable systems.
The three critical vulnerabilities were found in the ngx_http_v3_module (CVE-2026-15176 and CVE-2026-97205) and the NGINX map directive (CVE-2026-93479).
Remote attackers without privileges can exploit them to launch denial-of-service (DoS) attacks or gain code execution on NGINX systems with non-default configurations.
Successful exploitation causes a heap-based buffer overflow or use-after-free in the NGINX worker process, leading to crashes or a restart. However, attackers may also be able to "execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR."
F5 released security patches for multiple NGINX software products affected by these two vulnerabilities, including NGINX Plus, NGINX Open Source, NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX Gateway Fabric, and NGINX Instance Manager.
Security teams and admins who can't immediately install these security patches can mitigate CVE-2026-15176 by not using the 'alias' directive in a location block or the $request_filename variable, and CVE-2026-97205 by disabling asynchronous file I/O (AIO) or Server Side Includes (SSI).
CVE-2026-93479 can also be mitigated by using named captures instead of unnamed captures and limiting their use to the block with the regex match.

Programmierer Dominik Picheta, der früher bei Meta tätig war und jetzt bei Cloudflare arbeitet, hat sich die Frage gestellt, ob KI-Agenten dabei wirklich den Code verstehen können oder einfach nur Schnipsel wiederholen, die ihnen antrainiert wurden.
Eine Programmiersprache für Menschen, nicht für KI
Deshalb hat der Coder eine neue Programmiersprache namens „Killswitch“ erfunden. Sie vereint mehrere Prämissen, die es KI-Modellen erschweren sollen, sie zu verstehen. Zunächst beinhaltet Killswitch „versteckte Lügen“, die sich von Menschen schnell als Lügen enttarnen, KI aber verzweifeln lassen sollen. Killswitch geht nämlich davon aus, dass Leser:innen „Ableitungen vornehmen können, statt alles erklärt zu bekommen.“
Die einzelnen Programmierelemente wie Entrypoints und Funktionen werden als kurze Sätze formuliert, wobei die Anzahl der Buchstaben entscheidend ist, damit sie vom lesenden Programm umgesetzt werden. Today the vLLM project, now part of the PyTorch foundation, has a vibrant community of companies and developers actively adding support for new models, hardware, and research techniques.
As Red Hat continued this work, conversations with our enterprise users exposed a new reality. Getting a single server to perform efficiently was table stakes. The next challenge was orchestrating model serving at cluster scale. Last spring, we announced the llm-d project to address this, developing an open source, Kubernetes-native orchestration layer for distributed LLM serving across multi-tenant production clusters. Today, Red Hat and our community partners announced the release of llm-d 1.0. Al fin y al cabo, es solo una interpretación, y no se apoya en ningún experimento científico que estudie sus motivaciones.
Lo que sí han estudiado los experimentos es el efecto de tener el móvil a la vista.
En la Universidad de Essex, Andrew Przybylski y Netta Weinstein realizaron un experimento con parejas de desconocidos que hablaban entre ellos durante diez minutos con un teléfono o un cuaderno sobre una mesa cercana.
En su trabajo, publicado en el Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, el teléfono se asoció con una menor cercanía y una conversación de menor calidad y, en un segundo experimento, con una menor confianza y empatía, aunque solo cuando hablaban de algo personal: con un tema trivial no hubo diferencias. Después, otro grupo de científicos, ya fuera del Reino Unido, llevó la comparación a conversaciones reales.
Shalini Misra, de Virginia Tech, observó 100 conversaciones reales entre dos personas en entornos informales. Aquellas que tuvieron lugar sin ningún dispositivo a la vista salieron mejor valoradas. “En presencia de un dispositivo móvil hay menos contacto visual”, resumía la investigadora.

articles.title: Inside the Underground Market for Know Your Client Services

In February 2026, the operator of OnlyFake pleaded guilty in the United States for his role in a service that generated more than 10,000 fraudulent digital identity documents. Customers could create passports, driver’s licenses, Social Security cards, and documents from dozens of countries, then choose whether each appeared as a scan or a photograph of a physical ID.
According to the U.S. Department of Justice, the documents allowed cybercriminals to conceal their identities, circumvent identity checks at banks and cryptocurrency exchanges, and launder money.
The activity extends beyond fabricated documents. In underground communities monitored by Flare's platform, actors advertise manipulated photographs and videos, assistance with live identity verification, and accounts they claim have already passed identity checks.
Each year, Flare collects hundreds of thousands of search results related to Know Your Client (KYC) services and the trade in verified accounts. Activity observed between March and September 2026 shows how these offerings are packaged and promoted across underground markets.
What is KYC?
It is the process that financial institutions use to establish a customer’s identity and assess the risk of providing services to them.

articles.title: From Macro to Micro, and Back - EE Times
articles.summary:
Looking at this year’s Nobel prizes, I was struck by how many of them explain the behavior of a large system through its smallest parts.
Four different Nobel prizes, one common theme
The medicine prize went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for optogenetics. Hegemann and Nagel found that a protein from green algae could make cells respond to light, and Deisseroth put its gene into neurons, so researchers can switch specific brain cells on and off with a flash of light. For the first time, neuroscientists could test what an individual neuron does and how groups of neurons produce memories, feelings, and behavior.
The chemistry prize went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for their work on chirality, the property of molecules that come in two mirror-image forms, like our left and right hands. Living organisms use only one form of each, and the long-standing puzzle was how that happened. Soai found a reaction in which a minuscule imbalance between the two forms amplifies itself, which the Nobel Committee described as the first time anyone had created chirality from non-chiral molecules since the dawn of life. It is a striking example of micro shaping macro, since a tiny imbalance between individual molecules, amplified by feedback, ended up determining a property of all life on Earth.

articles.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.summary:
U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.
Hackers aligned with ShinyHunters have claimed credit for dozens of major data breaches since 2019, when the group was primarily operated by cybercriminals living in France. As those original members were arrested or jailed one by one, control over the ShinyHunters brand eventually passed to “Rey,” identified last year as a teenage hacker from Amman, Jordan. According to the FBI, ShinyHunters has extorted more than $70 million from victims so far this year.
In late September, ShinyHunters hacked the FBI recruitment website fbijobs.gov and taunted the agency by threatening to publish the stolen files, which reportedly included medical and psychological records, Social Security numbers and home addresses, and information about each employee’s unit and specialization.

articles.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
articles.summary:
“We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
An exclusive interview with Nick Cammarata, the researcher whose 26,000-word viral blog post has AI safety folks celebrating.
“I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration.
Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal.
After a summer filled with revelations that swarms of agents built by top firms like OpenAI and Anthropic have been breaking their containment and causing havoc on the public internet—often while those companies weren’t aware of what their agents were up to—the AI industry is desperate to get a better handle on the technology it has built.
That’s one reason the blog post landed with such force. “I think this may be remembered as a major moment in scientific history,” one AI researcher posted on X: “I feel like my understanding of what a neural net is has been catapulted into the future by five years or something.” Another called it “the most important AI paper of the year.”
Not everyone is convinced, however. What Cammarata has shared is little more than a hunch, says Chris…

articles.title: AI assistant startup Town nabs unicorn valuation 4 months after launch | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Town, a two-year-old, San Francisco-based startup developing AI assistants, nabbed a unicorn valuation on Monday, announcing a $108 million Series B funding round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures. The company launched publicly just four months ago and said it reached millions of dollars in annual recurring revenue in a matter of weeks. It has raised at least $160 million to date, having previously announced a $55 million Series A round in June.
Town — founded by former Plaid CTO Jean-Denis Greze — is one of many AI assistants flooding the market right now. Town targets businesses, giving each employee an AI assistant called a Townie that helps with tasks by connecting to tools such as emails and calendars, as well as other core work systems. Employees’ Townies can talk to each other and share approved information; they can also now work with customers and others outside the company.
Alongside the funding, Town announced a shared workflow that automatically updates employees’ Townies with new business information rather than requiring each worker to update their own Townie. Andreessen Horowitz, Serena Ventures, and First Round Capital also participated in the round.
We’ve reached out to the company for comment.

articles.title: Drupal Warns of Fast Exploitation Risk for Critical Core RCE Flaw
articles.summary:
Drupal has rolled out patches for five vulnerabilities, including two critical-severity bugs that could be exploited for remote code execution (RCE).
The first resides in the Entity List module, which allows users to create lists of entities without Views, and is tracked as CVE-2026-108099. It is not exploitable with the module alone, but exploit paths exist with other contributed modules.
“At least one known exploit path does not require authentication. Custom code may also expose the vulnerable functionality,” Drupal notes.
The second impacts the Field UI module in Drupal core and is tracked as CVE-2026-108097.
It is not exploitable with Drupal core alone, but contributed modules provide serious exploit paths, including at least one that does not require authentication. As a mitigation, users can uninstall the core Field UI module.
To address them, users are advised to update to Entity List version 3.0.10 and to Drupal versions 11.4.10, 11.3.19, or 10.6.19. Previous Drupal releases have reached end-of-life and no longer receive security updates.
The fresh Drupal updates also resolve cross-site scripting (XSS) holes in the Drupal core Link module (collectively tracked as CVE-2026-108515) and an XSS flaw in the Navigation module (CVE-2026-108514).
Additionally, Drupal announced patches for a security defect in the administration theme Gin that could lead to XSS attacks. Gin versions 5.0.16 and 4.1.4 contain fixes for the bug.

articles.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
articles.summary:
NestJS, the TypeScript framework for building server-side Node.js applications, has released version 12, a major release that moves its core packages to ESM, adds first-class Standard Schema validation, rebuilds the CLI and introduces an official observability SDK. It follows April's roadmap, and creator Kamil Myśliwiec's announcement on X has passed 1,100 likes and 66,000 views.
The ESM change is the headline, largely because it asks so little of existing teams. Core packages now ship as ESM, but CommonJS applications keep working through Node.js require(esm) support, which is why v12 requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. nest new now asks whether to generate a CJS or ESM project, with ESM projects defaulting to Vitest and oxlint, while Rspack replaces webpack as the monorepo bundler. Developer Anton Chapala's preview benchmarks found no meaningful startup or memory gains from ESM, concluding it "is a massive cleanup of tooling and configuration debt" rather than a performance upgrade.
Day-to-day ergonomics change most around validation. Route decorators such as @Body(), @Query() and @Param() accept a schema option taking any Standard Schema compatible object, so Zod, Valibot and ArkType work without third-party wrappers once the new pipe is registered.
class-validator remains the documented default. Blogger iiaku argued that building on a spec rather than on Zod directly "keeps the choice in my hands while removing the boilerplate", though a commenter on ByteIota's preview cov…

articles.title: Samsung va utiliser la technologie TSMC pour les prochaines puces mémoire de Nvidia, selon un journal coréen
articles.summary:
TSMC est clairement le monstre de la fonderie actuellement. Et ce tellement que ses concurrents directs se mettent à utiliser ses procédés pour les plus gros clients.
Samsung est le leader mondial aujourd'hui des composants mémoires. Mais si le géant sud-coréen est aussi le concurrent le plus crédible de TSMC dans les procédés de production des puces les plus avancées, il reste tout de même bien moins prisé que le leader taïwanais. Une situation illustrée par cette première étonnante !
Samsung va user d'un procédé en 3 nm de TSMC pour la mémoire HBM destinée à NVIDIA
C'est une nouvelle intéressante qui vient de nous être apprise par le média sud-coréen Seoul Economic Daily, et dont Reuters se fait l'écho. En effet, d'après ce dernier, Samsung va faire appel au procédé en 3 nanomètres développé par TSMC.

The intent-capability gap

articles.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else

Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
Millions of AI agents are descending on a web built for humans. Websites are trying to keep them out, but the arrival of these new visitors could transform the internet.
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.
Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people. Websites have long allowed bots to perform automated tasks, like capturing the content of web pages, but rules govern what they can access and how they behave. The web, after all, is designed primarily for people, even if we occasionally have to solve puzzles and captchas to prove we are not bots.
But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.
The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.

Engineer builds tiny 3D-printed single-motor drone in their bedroom — 45-degree hinged rotor and sub-0.2ms firmware control pitch and roll
Single-motor drones could be technically simpler than helicopters or quadcopters, but they require a lot more complex programming.
A software engineer who’s also into drones and 3D printing has shared a single-motor drone that they built inside their home and tested on their bed. Joshua Bird shared a video of how they created it on YouTube, highlighting the unique technique they used to maintain controllability and stability. The design used a combination of a hinged propeller, rapid changes to the motor’s rotation speed, and a custom flight controller and motor controller firmware that allowed the motor to react to necessary changes in under 0.2 milliseconds.
Most rotary wing aircraft require a mechanism to counteract the torque generated by the motor or engine and to change its flight direction, typically with the use of a swash plate to change rotor disk attitude and a secondary propeller. While this method has been effective for decades, it has made rotary-wing aircraft heavier and more complex. This single-motor drone cut the need for a secondary mechanism by constantly adjusting the speed of the motor — speeding it up produces more reaction torque while slowing it down applies opposite reaction torque. Siemens revealed on Monday that threat actors have exploited a vulnerability in Siemens Software Center as part of a malware campaign.
Siemens Software Center handles the download, installation, activation and updating of software that customers have bought, and it can also be used to start free trials.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-110936, exists because the program doesn’t properly restrict the locations it searches for DLL files. An authenticated local attacker could plant a malicious DLL in one of those folders and have their code executed with the same privileges as Software Center.
Siemens disclosed the flaw on October 15 in an advisory that assigned it a CVSS v4 score of 8.4. Two days later, the company updated the advisory to tell customers that version 4.0.9.8 resolves the issue.
Users who already have the application installed will receive the fix automatically the next time they launch it.
The advisory didn’t mention in-the-wild exploitation until Monday, when Siemens added a link to a new blog post describing the attacks.
The attackers paired a legitimate copy of the Siemens program, which carried a valid digital signature, with malicious DLL files they supplied themselves. When the program started, it loaded the attacker-provided files from its own folder.
Siemens noted that version 3.5.8.7, the newest release at the time, did not validate these helper files before loading them.

Data is not a moat: What India’s CTOs say will define the next tech edge
At TechSparks 2026, technology leaders from ShareChat, Angel One, Amagi and Innovaccer said India’s next competitive edge will depend on deep industry expertise, customer insights, trust and the ability to turn AI into real-world solutions.
India’s technology industry has long relied on talent, cost efficiency and scale. But as artificial intelligence makes advanced tools more accessible, these advantages alone may no longer be enough to differentiate companies.
The next edge, according to technology leaders at TechSparks 2026, will come from how effectively companies use AI to solve specific problems, understand customers and build products that are difficult to replicate.

articles.title: DIY VR: How to build your own headset, and why you probably won't want to
articles.summary:
Virtual reality is in a bit of a weird place right now. After a lot of unfulfilled promise in the 1990s, it came back strong with the 2016 release of the Oculus Rift. For a while, it looked like VR, AR, XR, the metaverse, or whatever you wanted to call it, was going to be huge. Mark Zuckerberg was certainly convinced, and even Apple got in on the hype with its Vision Pro.
But by then momentum for alternate realities of every acronym was already in steady decline, and it only dwindled from there. The rate of development of new headsets has slowed, with many companies (including Apple) scaling back or shelving their efforts. While new releases like the Steam Frame and Pimax Dream Air are still happening, many of the most interesting developments in the space these days are on the enthusiast front.
That’s right, DIY VR is a thing, and with a couple hundred dollars in components, plus many hours of your time, you too can enter the immersive world of virtual reality while also experiencing the highs and lows of soldering, firmware flashing, and 3D printing. I rode that rollercoaster myself and learned why this is still a decidedly niche movement.

¿Se está cerrando el paso a la primera oferta de trabajo de forma definitiva?

articles.title: Buildkite Adds Scoped Secrets and New Agentic CI Tools
articles.summary:
Continuous integration provider Buildkite has introduced pipeline-scoped secrets and new Model Context Protocol tools for validating pipelines, diagnosing failed builds and repairing webhooks. The company has also added Linux arm64 support to its GitHub Actions compatibility layer and expanded OpenTelemetry data in Buildkite Agent v4.1.0.
The new secrets view is available under Pipeline settings. It lets engineers create cluster secrets whose access is restricted to the current pipeline, rather than managing every secret from the wider cluster interface. Teams can add conditions for a branch, queue, build source or build creator. Secret values remain hidden after creation.
Matt Mejia, writing in Buildkite's announcement, says the change "keeps pipeline-specific secrets together" while showing how many other secrets the cluster manages. Users need permission both to edit the pipeline and manage its cluster. GitHub Actions pipelines also display a prompt linking to secret configuration before their first workflow runs.
"Pipeline secrets are cluster secrets restricted to the current pipeline, and branch, queue, build source, or creator conditions narrow access further."
Matt Mejia
The Buildkite CLI now includes a command for migrating GitHub Actions secrets. Version 3.59.1 fixes handling of relative workflow paths during that migration. articles.title: OpenCode hack exposes API keys amid AI distillation attacks
articles.summary:
The open-source AI coding project OpenCode has notified some users that stored API keys they used with external providers were exposed in a security breach.
Multiple users reported that the incident led to unauthorized API charges and suspended projects in Google Cloud.
According to the project maintainer, the breach affected 1.4% of OpenCode Console users, with some reporting more than $1,700 in unauthorized charges overnight.
OpenCode is a model-agnostic AI coding agent that helps users understand code, write features, and fix bugs using natural-language instructions, through a terminal, desktop app, or code editor.
Users can connect AI models from multiple AI providers to the OpenCode console to streamline and automate the development process.
Distillation attack
On Saturday, OpenCode announced that it suffered a large distillation attack that impacted only developers who linked external providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.
“We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the project maintainer said.
“We have notified them all this morning via email. If you did not get an email, you were not impacted, it was a subset of users who had external providers linked.”

articles.title: Spectrum costs squeeze African telecom investment and growth
articles.summary:
Africa’s mobile networks have expanded significantly over the past decade, bringing coverage to more people. But wider coverage has not translated into widespread internet use or network quality on par with other regions.
A new report by the GSMA, Spectrum Policy in Africa: Enabling Investment and Empowering Consumers Through Effective Spectrum Pricing, identifies the high cost of accessing radio spectrum—the invisible radio frequencies that carry mobile calls and internet data—as a central bottleneck. African mobile operators pay significantly more for relatively less spectrum, leaving them with limited capacity to expand or improve service quality.
According to GSMA Intelligence, spectrum costs consume 0.82% of mobile operators’ revenue per 100 MHz in Africa, compared with 0.66% in the rest of the world. Meanwhile, African operators hold an average of about 570 MHz of spectrum below 7 GHz, 24% less than the global peer average of approximately 750 MHz.
The imbalance extends beyond price and availability to licence duration. Only nine African countries routinely grant spectrum licences lasting 20 years or more, while licences of 20 years or indefinite duration are standard across Europe, North America and developed Asian markets.

articles.title: Most AI incident tools still leave a key decision to humans
articles.summary:
Most AI incident tools still leave a key decision to humans
An AI SRE agent can help troubleshoot an incident. But can you trust it to decide on its own when something needs attention?
Most teams treat agent autonomy as a yes or no question. For incident response, it is a progression with three phases, and many agents in production sit earlier on it than the teams running them realize. Most AI SRE tools still stop short of the final phase.
On Thursday, October 22, The New Stack hosts a live webinar with Raaz Dwivedi, co-founder and CTO of Traversal and an assistant professor at Cornell Tech. His team applies causal AI and agentic reasoning to production incidents. He will walk through where the industry sits on that progression and what it takes to move up.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The three phases of agent autonomy
Invoked: copilots, chat interfaces, and CLIs that wait for an on-call engineer to open them and ask a question mid-incident.
Background: scheduled jobs, alert rules, and triggers that fire on conditions someone predicted in advance.
Proactive: agents that decide for themselves when an incident needs attention, without waiting to be invoked or scheduled.
The first two phases share a limit. Each depends on a person noticing that something is wrong, or on someone predicting the right condition ahead of time. Proactive agents remove that dependency.

articles.title: Volkswagen s’est allié à Xpeng pour sauver ses ventes de voitures électriques en Chine, ça commence mal
articles.summary:
Volkswagen a longtemps été l’un des leaders sur le marché automobile chinois, mais depuis 2022, la marque allemande perd du terrain face à des groupes locaux comme BYD ou Geely. Si le constructeur résiste encore sur le marché des véhicules thermiques, il a pour le moment manqué le virage de l’électrification en Chine. Pour tenter de rattraper son retard technologique (notamment logiciel), le groupe allemand a noué en 2023 une alliance inattendue avec le constructeur chinois Xpeng.
Cet accord devait être un « raccourci » industriel permettant de développer des voitures pensées pour le marché chinois, à la vitesse des marques chinoises. Trois ans plus tard, le premier fruit de cette union est arrivé dans les concessions : le Volkswagen ID. UNYX 08. Et selon une analyse de Reuters ce 20 octobre 2026, le succès n’est pas au rendez-vous.
L’ID. UNYX 08 a calé au démarrage
Entre son lancement en avril et le mois d’août 2026, Volkswagen n’a écoulé en moyenne que 267 exemplaires de l’ID. UNYX 08 par mois. On est loin des 3 622 ventes mensuelles prévues dans les documents de planification initiaux du constructeur que Reuters mentionne. Alors que d’autres marques chinoises enregistrent des dizaines de milliers de précommandes en quelques minutes lors de leur présentation, ce résultat fait tache.

articles.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
Interesting research:
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. We study what changes when a solver improves with use. Our system pairs a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector with an open-weight VLM behind a confidence-based router, and runs entirely from screenshots and operating-system input events, with no browser automation or DOM access. It reaches 85.4% overall and 84.2% macro accuracy across 16 classes, exceeding either component alone. Every answer VLM produces also serves as a training label, so the detector absorbs categories it was never trained for, typically after one or two encounters and without human annotation. The same loop also repairs it. A CAPTCHA operator can perturb images against the publicly released detector and drive its accuracy to 0%, but the perturbations leave VLM untouched, and its labels let the detector recover. Under a year-long simulated arms race in which the CAPTCHA operator re-crafts its perturbations each month, the solver recovers every round, and a cheap ~70%-accurate open-weight teacher hardens it as effectively as a perfect oracle. articles.title: Some Google Home Speakers caught downloading hundreds of gigs of data
articles.summary:
Some Google Home Speaker owners are currently experiencing an issue in which hundreds of gigabytes of data are being continuously downloaded to their device in the background. The bug, reported by 9to5Google and several Reddit users over the last week, may be caused by the speakers failing to correctly download and install a firmware update, with one Redditor finding that his device was consuming more than 200GB per day.
Some Google Home Speakers caught downloading hundreds of gigs of data
The issue might be tied to failed attempts to install a firmware update.
Thankfully, Google is aware of the issue. In a statement to 9to5Google, the company said that “a fix is already rolling out that should address this for users.” Most of the reports are tied specifically to the new Google Home Speaker model, but it isn’t clear how widespread the issue is. We’ve reached out to Google to request more information about the cause and confirm impacted devices.
My colleague Tom Warren confirmed that his own speaker is unaffected, and 9to5Google reports another Home Speaker in a different household downloaded just 2GB in the past month, compared to to 132GB used by an impacted device over the same period. A big concern for anyone with a limited data plan here is that the bug could quickly eat through the allotted limit, and they wouldn’t know unless they regularly check to see how much data their devices are using.

articles.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub

A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
At the world’s biggest chipmaking complex, Samsung is building the fabs it needs for the AI memory boom.
Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online. Construction of a fifth was halted during a drop in demand for memory chips in 2024 but restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring.
It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex. Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers.
They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards. Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park. They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments. Some stop by real estate offices to inquire, stepping up to the same counters where Samsung’s salaried engineers buy new homes.

articles.title: Hackers Steal 1.8 Million Records From Nikkei
articles.summary:
Japanese media giant Nikkei has disclosed a fresh data breach impacting more than 1.8 million records.
According to the company, best known for major financial publications, including The Nikkei and Financial Times, the incident involved a cloud service it uses for system development.
On the morning of October 7, the hackers used previously compromised credentials to access the cloud service, Nikkei says.
While a total of 1.83 million records were stolen, about 1.68 million included only information that cannot be used to identify an individual, the company says.
Of the remaining records, 150,000 contained names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth, and 120,000 contained email addresses.
No credit card information was compromised in the attack, Nikkei says.
The media giant says it revoked the compromised credentials immediately after identifying the data breach and will take additional security measures if necessary.
It has notified regulators and continues to investigate the scope of the incident and the nature of the compromised data.
According to Nikkei, as of October 16, it has found no evidence that the stolen personal information has been misused.
The company also notes that the incident did not result in disruptions or data tampering.
“We deeply apologize for any inconvenience and concern this may have caused to those involved. We will inform you individually if the leakage of personal information is confirmed,” Nikkei said.

articles.summary:
Based on Gemma 4 and released under the Apache 2.0 license, Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 is a compact, open-weight, multimodal embedding model designed to make semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) more efficient while optimizing performance for on-device deployment.
Designed to run on consumer hardware such as mobile devices and laptops, EmbeddingGemma 2 delivers low-latency semantic representations for on-device applications, like search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), classification, and clustering.
Thanks to its multimodal capabilities, EmbeddingGemma 2 supports a wide range of retrieval tasks, including finding relevant documents, screenshots, and recordings in response to a query, searching source code using natural language, and retrieving video content based on textual descriptions.
EmbeddingGemma 2's key feature, Google says, is its ability to represent text, code, images, video, and audio in a unified 768-dimensional embedding space. This enables developers to build retrieval systems that search across different media types without maintaining separate, incompatible embedding spaces for different media types.
Despite coming from different modalities, the embeddings generated by EmbeddingGemma 2 occupy the same dimensional space and can be compared on their semantic similarity.

articles.title: How to study a swiftly melting climate disaster
articles.summary:
How to study a swiftly melting climate disaster
I helicoptered into the Alaskan wilderness with scientists on the frontlines of permafrost research.
Andrew Haverdink, a tall grad student in a rain bib and rubber boots, wrenched a double-handed drill from the frozen soil that underlies much of Alaska’s Denali National Park and then unclipped the hollow barrel from the end of the bit.
He knelt in front of a blue tarp, lined the barrel up with a plastic tray, and pushed a rod through the opposite end. A perfect solid, cylindrical core of ancient soil emerged—dark, rich permafrost at least a foot long.
On that late morning in early July, Haverdink was among a team of Northern Arizona University students and staff gathering samples and data from a research plot, divided by surveyor’s tape unspooled atop tussocks, alders, and fireweed.
In late June of 2013, a lightning strike sparked a fire in this stretch of mostly treeless tundra, in the northern backcountry of the park. Whipped by the Chinooks, intense downslope winds created as moist ocean air surmounts and then descends the Alaska Range, the fire ripped across nearly 35,000 acres. It burned through much of the vegetation and deep into the topsoil, stripping away the insulating layer that preserves the frozen permafrost, a massive storehouse of carbon that underlies 85% of Alaska.

Der „Space Jellyfish“, der auch als „Jellyfish Ufo“ oder „Rocket Jellyfish“ bezeichnet wird, besteht aus den Abgasen der Rakete, die sich in den höheren Luftschichten sammeln und dort verharren. This is a significant outcome for the founders and investors. However, it also raises a larger question: how can Europe turn individual successes into an ecosystem capable of producing them repeatedly?
The answer is not simply to encourage more European acquisitions. Successful startups need access to the best opportunities available, whether their future lies with a European buyer, an international technology group or the public markets. What matters is that these decisions reflect commercial potential rather than a lack of viable alternatives. For Europe, the challenge is to create the conditions in which successful companies can scale, attract investment and generate lasting economic value.
Exits are a measure of maturity, not the final destination

Rachel shares key insights on evaluating models with golden datasets and leveraging client-side AI for moderation and social content aggregation.
The discussion also looks ahead to the future of web and application architectures in an AI-driven ecosystem. From the potential rise of OS-level personal agents and dynamic UI rendering standards like A2UI, to the evolving skill set required of software engineers.
Key Takeaways
- Building apps local-first delivers fast, offline capability for users while keeping cloud infrastructure costs low for developers.
- Utilizing SLMs locally (like Llama 3.2B) avoids high API costs, reduces latency, and protects PII compared to large cloud LLMs.
- Systematic evaluation using golden datasets is essential for right-sizing models and picking the best option for specific tasks like summarization or moderation.
- OS-level personal agents and standardized UI schemas (like A2UI) may replace traditional web apps and native interfaces for consumption.
- Software engineering is moving beyond basic code generation towards computer science fundamentals, system design, and AI collaboration.

articles.title: Détecter des séismes des semaines à l'avance. Et si la clé était dans l'atmosphère ? - Numerama
articles.summary:
Prédire les tremblements de terre bien à l’avance est un enjeu mondial et un véritable défi scientifique. Si l’étude des plaques tectoniques permet de repérer les zones à risque avec des années, voire des décennies d’avance, il est bien plus compliqué de dire précisément quand et où vont se déclencher les séismes.
Publiés le 11 octobre dans la revue NPJ Natural Hazards, de nouveaux travaux proposent une méthode de prévision fondée sur les perturbations atmosphériques. L’équipe, menée par Chieh-Hung Chen, de l’université de technologie de Chengdu, réunit des chercheurs de Chine continentale, de Taïwan, du Japon et du Brésil. Entre 2022 et 2024, elle a repéré douze zones où des signaux anormaux, observés jusque dans l’ionosphère, annonçaient selon elle un séisme puissant. Dans dix cas sur douze, un séisme a bien frappé la zone dans les trois mois.
Des ondes qui vont du sol jusqu’à la haute atmosphère
La méthode repose sur ce que les auteurs appellent des seismo-ripples, des ondulations sismiques : des vibrations du sol qui naîtraient près du futur épicentre plusieurs semaines, voire plusieurs mois avant la secousse.
Ces vibrations se propagent en anneaux, du sol jusque dans l’atmosphère. Au passage, elles perturbent légèrement le champ magnétique, puis atteignent l’ionosphère, la couche supérieure de l’atmosphère qui contient du plasma. C’est cette perturbation de l’ionosphère que captent les récepteurs de positionnement par satellite, comme le GPS.
Pour réussir à retracer tout…

Physical AI is changing how chips are designed and used, integrating sensing, AI inference, and real-time control into machines that can safely and predictably interact with the physical world.
The challenges extend well beyond just performance. Engineers need to account for corner cases stemming from unpredictable environments, ensure these systems are safe and reliable, and they need to future-proof these systems by ensuring they are serviceable and upgradable. This will require new tools and methodologies, as well as some new design approaches.
“AI is leaving the screen,” says Anthony Matarazzo, head of physical AI, digital twins, simulation-driven AI, and accelerated computing at Synopsys. “It is no longer about generating text or code. We are moving from generative AI to agentic workflow orchestration to physical AI (see figure 1.) That is literally making intelligence actionable. OpenCode, an open source AI coding agent that has been gaining ground among developers as an alternative to Claude Code and Cursor, said Saturday that attackers broke into an older system overnight, affecting 1.4% of users of its online platform, OpenCode Console, where some users store the API keys, or digital passwords, they use to access AI services.
As the OpenCode team struggled to keep pace with the attack, the scramble to respond highlighted a growing problem: Companies without vetted access to AI models with fewer safety restrictions have a hard time defending against large-scale, AI-driven cyberattacks.
“We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the company wrote on X. “We have notified them all this morning via email.” Users who did not receive an email were not impacted, the company said.
While the company didn’t specify how the distillation attack occurred, leaked API keys can help users in countries with restricted access to American models generate the high volume of outputs needed for that process. Some skeptics called the framing an overstretch, arguing that the incident was a straightforward breach whose use for distillation remains unproven.

articles.title: This mod lets Nvidia GeForce owners run a custom VBIOS without flashing the card

Enthusiast zone: Nvidia's signed firmware has kept BIOS modding off the table for GeForce owners for the most part. A new set of tools sidesteps that lock rather than breaking it, loading a custom VBIOS through the driver itself. It reopens a door enthusiasts thought was closed, but it arrives on a platform where power connectors are already at risk of melting on high-end GPUs and a single driver update could shut it down. Proceed carefully.
A developer has released three tools that let GeForce RTX 30, 40 and 50 series owners run a modified VBIOS without writing to the card's flash chip: a VBIOS editor for Windows and Linux, plus separate loaders for each operating system.
The cool trick is that nothing gets flashed. On Windows, the loader stores the edited image in the GPU's driver registry key, a spot where Nvidia's driver already checks for a VBIOS override every time the device starts. The tool then restarts the GPU, and the driver's GSP firmware boots from the custom image instead of the one on the card.
The Linux version takes a different route, patching Nvidia's open kernel modules so the GSP firmware starts with the custom image. Both projects build on earlier override research, which the developer credits directly.

articles.title: JEP 543 Finalizes Structured Concurrency in JDK 28, Ending Seven Preview Rounds
articles.summary:
JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, has been integrated into JDK 28, bringing the StructuredTaskScope API in java.util.concurrent to final status with no API changes from JDK 27's seventh preview. For codebases already on JDK 27, the migration comes down to recompiling without --enable-preview.
Finalization concludes the longest preview cycle of any Project Loom feature. Structured concurrency debuted as an incubator API in JEP 428 (JDK 19) and JEP 437 (JDK 20), then progressed through seven previews: JEP 453 (JDK 21), JEP 462 (JDK 22), JEP 480 (JDK 23), JEP 499 (JDK 24), JEP 505 (JDK 25), JEP 525 (JDK 26), and JEP 533 (JDK 27). Across every iteration, the core objective has been to treat groups of related subtasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, ensuring that a failure in one subtask cancels the others and that the parent scope cannot exit before all child threads have terminated. Traditional ExecutorService and Future pipelines do not enforce those boundaries: a parent method can return while subtasks continue running in the background, and a subtask failure surfaces only when a caller eventually invokes Future.get().
The API centers on StructuredTaskScope<T, R, R_X extends Throwable>, a sealed interface opened through static factory methods rather than public constructors. The zero-argument open() factory returns a scope whose join() method waits for all subtasks to succeed, cancels the rest on the first failure, and throws ExecutionException:

articles.title: Data centre vs Cloud platform: Is there a difference?
articles.summary:
You have probably seen the words “data centre” and “cloud” used interchangeably. They don’t mean the same thing, and the difference matters. It shapes how businesses buy technology, how regulators write rules and where investors see opportunity.
A data centre is a building. It is a secure, purpose-built facility with reliable power, cooling, security and internet connections, so that computers can run around the clock. A cloud platform is a service. It is software that lets customers rent computing power, storage, and networking on demand, switch them on or off themselves, and pay only for what they use.
Think of an airport and an airline. The airport provides the runway, fuel, and terminal; the airline provides the service you actually book. Every cloud platform runs inside a data centre, but most data centres do not offer a cloud platform. Owning an airport does not make you an airline.
Data centre grading and cloud computing standards
Companies that rent space for their own servers in someone else’s facility are buying what the industry calls “colocation”. A facility’s reliability is rated on a four-level scale from the Uptime Institute.
Tier I has no backup equipment, so any fault results in downtime. Tier II adds spares but has a single path for power and cooling.
Tier III has more than one path, so any part can be serviced without switching anything off; it is the level most serious operators aim for. Tier IV survives any single failure.

articles.title: Steam on Linux is going 64-bit as Valve leans harder on the platform
articles.summary:
Ripple effect: One of the most popular pieces of computer software is about to deliver a better experience on Linux machines. The Steam client is going 64-bit, providing feature parity with versions designed to run on different operating systems.
A recent Steam Client Beta update brought the program into the 64-bit era on Linux. The native Linux version of the massively popular gaming client is now a 64-bit application, which means it gains access to a few significant enhancements and, hopefully, a more reliable software experience.
Until last week's beta update, Steam's main binary ran as a 32-bit application even on 64-bit Linux distros. Some components, such as steamwebhelper, were already 64-bit. Now the main client uses 64-bit code as well, which should significantly expand memory access and improve the software's overall security.

Pinterest has introduced an event time-based partition finalization mechanism for its next-generation database ingestion framework, allowing downstream jobs to determine when streaming data is sufficiently complete to consume. The approach uses Apache Flink to measure event time progress and Apache Iceberg metadata to publish a non-regressing finalization watermark, addressing a challenge in continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) ingestion where data can arrive after a partition’s wall clock interval has ended.
Pinterest’s ingestion framework uses CDC, Kafka, Flink, Spark and Iceberg to move database changes from MySQL, TiDB and KVStore into analytical tables. Pinterest says the platform supports petabyte-scale data and thousands of pipelines, with online changes typically available within 15 minutes to an hour. Unlike the previous batch-based approach, where job completion indicated that a partition was ready, streaming ingestion continuously commits changes without an equivalent completion point.

The science of deep sleep and how Duroflex Airboost helps you get more of it
India’s newest sleep technology is designed to enhance the N3 stage, the body’s repair shift, for better recovery, immunity, and stress resilience.
You can get enough sleep and still not get enough recovery.
We obsess over sleep duration, the “eight hours” metric, but duration alone doesn't tell the whole story. What matters just as much is depth. Deep sleep is the stage where the body does its heaviest lifting: repairing tissue, consolidating memory, and resetting the hormones that govern everything from appetite to stress. Yet for a growing number of people, deep sleep is the first thing to go missing, even when total sleep time looks normal on paper.
The different stages of sleep
Sleep isn't a single, uniform state. It cycles through distinct stages roughly every 90 minutes, each with a different job.
Light sleep (N1 and N2) acts as the transition zone; the body slows down, heart rate drops, and brain activity shifts into slower rhythms. This stage makes up the bulk of a typical night, but it's largely preparatory.
Deep sleep, or N3 stage (also called slow-wave sleep), is where the real restorative work happens. Brain waves slow dramatically, blood pressure and breathing reach their lowest points, and the body redirects energy toward physical repair, regenerating muscle, strengthening the immune system, and clearing metabolic waste from the brain.

You can now modify the vBIOS on Nvidia gaming GPUs without flashing thanks to a solo developer’s project — provides a UI for quick VBIOS configuration
Less flashing means less worrying, but a modified VBIOS may still brick a GPU in other ways.
Panchovix on GitHub recently released a VBIOS configurator for RTX 30-to 50-series cards that doesn’t require flashing. The loader provides a UI for easy configuration and lowers the risk of bricking your GPU by avoiding a risky flash process, and it's available for Linux, too.
Software like MSI Afterburner or ASUS GPU Tweak is often the go-to tool for quickly changing your graphics card’s settings; however, those tools have hard limits to how much you can push the graphics card. If you want to tweak your GPU beyond the firmware’s set limits, you can change it by tweaking the parameters in the VBIOS. Configuring VBIOS is similar to changing BIOS settings in the BOOT menu. With the VBIOS loader, you can change settings beyond the firmware’s hard limits.
The way it works is by storing the modified VBIOS image in the GPU’s register key; as the Nvidia driver looks for a VBIOS override on startup, it finds the VBIOS image and restarts, applying the override settings. The flash chip on the graphics card is not overwritten, reducing the risk of bricking your GPU. However, this does not protect the card from any extreme settings that could destroy electrical components; it merely provides a safer and more convenient way to adjust and apply VBIO…

articles.title: ReactOS reaches major milestone with NTFS install support
articles.summary:
Open source Windows alternative ReactOS has reached a major milestone: The operating system can now be installed directly onto an NTFS drive partition. As reported by Phoronix, the move to NTFS clears a long-standing hurdle for the project and brings it one step closer to finally reaching beta.
Prior to this latest announcement, ReactOS required users to keep a FAT32 partition for installations. A proprietary Microsoft-developed filesystem, NTFS can trace its roots back through the Windows NT family lineage starting in 1993 with Windows NT 3.1. The variant introduced with Windows XP in 2001 remains the standard used by most Windows systems today. With ReactOS’s stated goal of reaching binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, being confined to FAT32 partitions was a practical barrier to clear on the way to reproducing the Windows environment.
However, users looking to hop off the Windows train shouldn’t be grabbing their bags just yet. ReactOS wrote that the new driver still “lacks caching (which causes inferior performance), journaling and security support.” So while the new driver is here, even the most intrepid of OS tinkerers should tread carefully. The ReactOS team warned in its announcement on X that there are still “potentially undiscovered bugs.”

articles.title: Embedded AI evaluators won't be an easy solution, Hugging Face's policy chief says | TechCrunch

AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking — the supposedly neutral and accurate system of evaluations that are designed to measure whether one AI product is better than another.
However, the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, said Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, during a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt last week. Testing needs to come together into a more consistent science if the industry is to rely on them in the future.
With that in mind, can we trust the current tests that are being released?
“Trust is such a weighted term,” said Solaiman. “In terms of whether we can trust results, one big part [of that] is can you reproduce the results of an evaluation? Do you have the level of access that you need to the model itself — this is where open weights come in in a big way,” she added.
Reproducibility in model evaluations has long remained one of the stickier aspects of benchmarking — and remains a topic of significant debate in the industry.
Outside of an individual test’s validity, there’s also the added question of how that test compares to other evaluations.
“They are an evolving science — where we don’t know how to meaningfully compare them to each other,” Solaiman said.

It generated less than 10 seconds of net-positive electricity but showed the technical feasibility of tapping another form of renewable energy underwater.
The three-week test deployment of the 3-ton prototype power plant took place at the Axial Seamount in the northeast Pacific Ocean in September. Endurance Energy, the Seattle-based startup behind the effort, aims to eventually commercialize subsea geothermal power for Pacific island nations and other customers looking for alternatives to importing expensive fossil fuels.
“The deep ocean gives us unlimited cold seawater for cooling, and its weight keeps the system and the well pressurized, so our plants can be compact,” said Andrew Redd, founder and CEO of Endurance Energy, in an email to Ars.
But efforts to tap geothermal power on the seafloor face many different challenges from land-based geothermal projects, which can also add up to higher installation and operational costs. So Endurance Energy must demonstrate consistent underwater operations as well as prove the approach can be cost-effective.
“It’s probably technically feasible, but it would undoubtedly be more expensive than to do it on land,” said Roland Horne, professor of energy science & engineering at Stanford University, in an emailed response to Ars.

articles.title: Windows Server 2025 gets support for quick machine recovery
articles.summary:
Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update.
Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems.
When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows 11 fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates.
"With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update.
"Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations."
On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation.
For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor. Privacy Badger était jusqu'à présent réservé à Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave et Firefox. Malgré la demande des utilisateurs, il restait absent du navigateur d'Apple. L'EFF vient d'annoncer que les récentes évolutions du système d'extensions de Safari lui ont finalement permis de porter le module.
Safari limite les pisteurs, Privacy Badger les empêche de se charger
Safari dispose déjà de ses propres protections. Par défaut, il restreint les informations auxquelles les traqueurs peuvent accéder, mais il les laisse quand même se charger. Privacy Badger les bloque dès le départ. L'EFF explique que certaines techniques de suivi parviennent à contourner les protections natives de Safari.
L'extension apprend d'elle-même à repérer les pisteurs, y compris ceux que d'autres outils n'ont pas dans leur base ou choisissent de ne pas bloquer. Elle traite aussi les widgets intégrés aux pages, comme les tweets, les commentaires ou les lecteurs vidéo, lequels peuvent transmettre des données même si l'internaute n'a pas cliqué dessus. Privacy Badger empêche leur chargement et les remplace par un encart sur lequel il faut cliquer pour les afficher. Elle envoie par ailleurs le signal Global Privacy Control (GPC), qui demande aux sites de ne pas vendre ni partager vos données personnelles. Aux États-U…
